set.st: Heinrich Maas of Cooperstown left a will that disposed of a pot of gold he had buried; its place was written on a slip of paper kept in his watch case. When the estate looked, the hole the pot had sat in was found, but the gold was gone. Estate attorneys Schenian & Kelley cited William Maas before Judge Anderson on 21 Mar 1898 'to tell what he knows about the gold'; no outcome was reported in 1898-99. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself.
src: Manitowoc Pilot, Feb. 17 and Mar. 17, 1898 (Mar. 17, p. 3: Newspapers.com 900613190)
set.tovw: D: hole found empty in 1898, pot gone; probably taken by family; no later report
set.t: Probably taken: the hole was found, the pot was not. Record only unless the probate file says otherwise. Farm not placed (not on the 1893 plate). Permission: private farm land, ask first.

pinev: Superior directories 1889-96 list only an Adolph Strobel; possibly the same man under a variant spelling. Not placed.

Superior Evening Telegram and Superior Times are indexed for 1897-98 but carry no local story under Strolfer, Strobel or 'hermit'; the name is probably OCR-mangled. Location stays the wire's '4 mi E of Superior'.
